content.text:
I fixed the stack overflow. With a top-level variable named `set`, both examples from the issue now compile to working code. The helpers, `transform-classes`, `transform-object-super` and `@babel/core` test suites all pass (675 passed, 1 skipped).

**Cause:** the fix is in `permuteHelperAST` in `packages/babel-helpers/src/index.ts`. The `set` helper has an inner function `set` and an exported function `_set`. When it was injected, the inner `set` was renamed to `_set` to avoid the user's variable. The code that picks those new names never checked the helper's own exported name, so the inner function took the same name as the export and `_set` ended up calling itself.

**Fix:** before renaming a helper's inner names, I now reserve two more names: the exported function's original name and the name it's being renamed to. Each newly chosen name is also reserved, so two inner names can't end up with the same new name. In the output from the issue, the inner function is now `__set` and the exported `_set` calls `__set`.

This is a general fix in the helper-injection code, not a special case for `set`, so it covers any helper with an inner/exported pair like `xxx` and `_xxx`, which the issue asked about. I didn't add a regression test.
